To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) in the overlapping-generations model with one agent per generation, no monetary competitive equilibrium is in the competitive core; (2) for the case of a large number of goods, the value of monetary transactions in competitive equilibria belonging to the competitive core must be bounded from above by some positive constant; (3) in a large number of economies the competitive core is nonempty.

(1) for economies with one agent per generation the set of core allocations is characterized by a system of inequalities, which are easy to compute; (2) for economies with many goods, no money equilibrium is in the Core, unless the number of generations is bounded from above; (3) for economies with two goods and many agents per generation the value of money transfers in competitive equilibria must be bounded from below.

(i) the core is a subset of the set of competitive equilibria; (ii) for economies with one agent per generation no monetary equilibrium is an element of the core; and (iii) in economies with many goods the core is bounded by the set of competitive allocations.
